title: Dynamic policy synthesizer for per-route & per-customer safe rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a policy synthesizer service that consumes per-route and per-customer traffic metrics and outputs safe, staged configuration changes (batching, prefix/KV cache TTLs, allowlists/denylists, and tier templates). The synthesizer should produce a policy delta, validate it via shadow/dry-run, suggest confidence scores and rollback triggers, and push staged changes through the existing rollout service with automated guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Synthesizer produces a human-readable policy delta for a sample customer and two routes
Dry-run simulation predicts >=15% token-cost reduction for at least one route without exceeding 2x latency p95 in simulated traffic
Generated policies include explicit allowlist/denylist entries or tier-assignment recommendations
Rollout path integrates with rollout API and supports canary percent, watch windows, and automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches
End-to-end integration test in staging validates apply->monitor->rollback flow with synthetic traffic
implementation_notes: Use existing metrics in BigQuery -> feature-extract pipeline for route-level QPS, median latency, p95 latency, token distribution, and cache hit rate
Policy delta schema: flat key-value changes + metadata (confidence, reason, simulated-impact-ids, suggested-watch-window) - store as JSON string in policy-store
Shadow mode: route requests forwarded to quantizer that simulates additional batching/caching settings without affecting production outputs
Safety fences: per-customer allowlist/denylist precedence, max-batching-limit per tier, and conservative defaults for low-traffic routes
Scoring model: lightweight heuristic that weights cost-savings vs latency-risk; include monotonicity test to avoid oscillation
Telemetry: emit policy.proposed, policy.applied, policy.rollback events with tags for route, customer, and rollout_id
progress: 2026-03-10: Kickoff - aligned on goals with PM and Design; scoped 8 points; agreed to reuse rollout API
2026-03-12: PoC completed - synthesizer prototype generates policy deltas from historical traffic (saves ~18% tokens in simulation)
2026-03-13: Design review - Design suggested adding clear user-facing rationale in the delta ("why this change") and an opt-out flag for customers
2026-03-14: Security review stubbed - confirmed no cryptographic changes; will add audit log entries for every change
risks: Overly aggressive batching could violate latency SLOs for tail-sensitive routes
Automated policy churn if scoring model reacts to short-term spikes; add smoothing and min-change window
Incorrect allowlist/denylist updates could unintentionally throttle VIP customers - require manual approval for tiered VIP lists
Dependency on rollout service readiness for automatic rollback - fallback to manual alerts if unavailable
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dry-run - run synthesizer in read-only mode across sampled customers for 72h
Phase 1: Shadow apply for low-impact routes (<=1 req/s) for 48h with logging only
Phase 2: Canary apply 5% traffic for a single customer segment (bronze tier) with 30m watch windows
Phase 3: Gradual expansion by doubling canary every 24h if no SLO regressions
Phase 4: Full apply for route after 7 successful canary windows
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency > baseline * 1.5 OR error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute within watch window
Immediate rollback action: revert policy delta via rollout API and notify on-call + PM
Manual rollback: provide UI button with pre-filled rollback delta and incident template
Post-rollback analysis: synthesize root cause and adjust scoring thresholds before next attempt
qa_plan: Create synthetic workloads for three customer profiles (low, medium, bursty)
Run integration test that asserts rollback triggers fire under injected latency faults
Smoke test for audit logging, ensuring every applied delta is recorded and queryable
User acceptance: product review of the "why this change" rationale and opt-out flow
notes: Follow-up: determine retention window for proposed policy events (30 days vs 90 days)
Consider future work: automated tier reassignment based on long-term cost/latency trends
Related: coordinate with Dedicated infra team to ensure dedicated pools honor per-customer cache TTLs
